messages:
olivia: Quick design review request  copy for the 'Delete API key' confirmation modal. Security wants the consequences clearer. Thinking aloud: current secondary is 'Cancel' which could be ambiguous. Also need tooltip text for the 'Delete' button explaining irreversible effects.

sam: Thanks! Can you paste the current modal copy?

olivia: Sure:
```
Title: Delete API key?
Body: This will remove the key from your account.
Primary: Delete
Secondary: Cancel
```

kai: That's a little light on detail. Users need to know if there are active services using the key and whether deletion revokes tokens immediately. Suggest: body include "This will immediately revoke any tokens tied to this key and may break running integrations."

devraj: From an infra perspective, deletion is immediate and revocation happens at auth check time. We can add a line: "Requests using the key will fail after deletion."

olivia: Good call. What about microcopy on the primary button? Right now it's just 'Delete' which is fine but maybe 'Delete API key' is clearer and verb-first.

sam: I like 'Delete API key' as the primary. For the secondary, avoid generic 'Cancel' — propose 'Keep key' or 'Don't delete'. 'Keep key' reads better imo.

kai: Accessibility note: buttons should be descriptive when read by screen readers. 'Delete' alone is ambiguous if there are multiple delete actions on the page. Use 'Delete API key' for aria-label.

design-bot: Automated check: prefer explicit action labels for confirmation dialogs. Recommend primary: 'Delete API key' and secondary: 'Keep key'. Also suggest adding a short consequence sentence in plain language.

olivia: Draft candidates for body copy:
A) "This will immediately revoke the key. Any running services using it may stop working."
B) "Deleting this key revokes access instantly. You may need to update integrations to restore access."
C) "This action cannot be undone. Keys revoked now will stop any in-progress requests."

sam: My vote B  it's actionable and suggests next steps. A is ok but 'may stop working' feels weak. C is fine but 'in-progress requests' might be misleading.

devraj: I'd avoid promising anything about in-progress requests; our system doesn't guarantee allowing in-flight requests to complete. So B is safer.

olivia: Ok B it is. For the tooltip on the delete button (hover state), thinking: "Deletes key and revokes access immediately. This cannot be undone." Short, but need to ensure it's read by assistive tech. Maybe expose same text in aria-describedby.

kai: Agree, use aria-describedby to associate the tooltip content or an offscreen description. Also add role="alertdialog" on the modal since it's destructive and needs focus trap.

sam: Analytics: track both confirm and cancel variants. If we rename secondary to 'Keep key', change event label from 'confirm_cancel' to 'keep_key_clicked' to avoid ambiguity.

olivia: I'll update the design system modal component to accept full string labels and an optional consequence line. Proposed final copy:
Title: "Delete API key?"
Body: "Deleting this key revokes access instantly. You may need to update integrations that rely on it."
Primary: "Delete API key" (aria-label="Delete API key")
Secondary: "Keep key" (aria-label="Keep key")
Tooltip: "Deletes the key and revokes access immediately. This cannot be undone." (exposed via aria-describedby)

devraj: Implementation check: we'll add server-side log for deletion time and key id to help recovery/audit. Also ensure we block deletion of system-managed keys via UI.

kai: Also add an inline link in the modal to doc: "How to rotate keys" so users have a next step. Maybe small link under the body: 'Learn how to rotate keys'.

olivia: Good idea  small link text: "Learn how to rotate keys" (opens /docs/keys#rotate).

sam: Action items: olivia -> update DS modal variant and visuals; devraj -> ensure aria-describedby and audit logging; kai -> review wording for legal/security; i'll update analytics events. I'll review once the PR is up. :thumbsup:

olivia: Thanks all! I'll post updated screenshot and copy in the thread once done. :sparkles:
